title: Wajdi and the Unlit Room
logline: Wajdi descends into Farah and learns the dark was only unremembered light.
story: Everyone warned that Farah, who was joy, could not be reached — the way down was made of everything Wajdi had refused to remember. Wajdi, who carried the ecstasy of finding, standing beyond the self, went looking anyway. So instead of fighting the dark, Wajdi sat in it and listened — and the dark, for the first time, was not afraid of being seen. When Wajdi rose, nothing outside had changed, and everything had. The darkness had not been an enemy; it was only a room with the light switched off, waiting for someone unhurried enough to find the switch within.
moral: The darkness is not the absence of light, but light that has not yet been remembered.
